subject: Human Body
title: Ligaments and Tendons
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Ligaments and Tendons.

hook.text: Ligaments tie bone to bone. Tendons tie muscle to bone. Both are tough cords you can't see but always use.

buildup.text: Ligaments stabilize joints. The ACL in your knee keeps the shin bone from sliding forward.

discovery.text: Tendons transmit force. The Achilles tendon can handle loads of 1,000 pounds during a sprint.

twist.text: Ligaments stretch very little. If forced too far, they tear. A torn ACL rarely heals on its own.

climax.text: Tendons are elastic but not invincible. Overuse causes tendinitis, one of the most common sports injuries.

punchline.text: Invisible cords hold your skeleton together. Snap one and you know.
